rooms.2318: The heath gives out against a long wall of grey fieldstone, and the Dusty Road turns sharply north to follow it. Old flagstones show through the dust here, laid by some long-forgotten road-builder and heaved apart by frost. A rusted iron ring is set into the wall at the corner, perhaps for tethering horses in busier days. West, the road runs back across the heather toward the village, its thatch just visible above the gorse.
rooms.2319: A wayside post stands at this bend, crowned with a disc of beaten tin cut in the shape of a sun and dulled by rain. Someone still tends it: a fresh braid of garlic hangs from a nail, and pebbles have been laid in a careful ring around its foot. The Dusty Road swings east here between low walls, and runs back south along the fieldstone wall to the corner. The wind off the heath sets the garlic swinging.
rooms.2320: The road runs straight between walls of piled stone, past the shell of a farmhouse whose roof has fallen in upon its own rafters. Its fields have gone to thistle and dock, and a plough lies rusting in the furrow where it was last left. No smoke rises anywhere in sight. East, the road carries on toward a line of tall elms, and west it bends back toward the sun-post.
rooms.2321: A squat milestone of red sandstone leans at the roadside, its face cut with letters that someone has tried hard to chisel away. Tall elms begin here, planted in a row along the verge long ago, and their roots have lifted the edge of the road into ridges. The dust lies thinner in their shade. The Dusty Road runs on east beneath the elms and back west past the ruined farm.
rooms.2322: An old gibbet stands at this corner of the road, a tall black post with an arm from which an empty iron cage hangs on a chain. The cage creaks when the wind moves it, and the grass beneath has never grown back. Whoever last hung there is long forgotten, though the ground below is still strewn with salt. The road turns north here under the last of the elms and runs back west along their line.
rooms.2323: A low wall of mossy stone encloses a small graveyard beside the road, entered by a roofed lychgate whose timbers have gone silver with age. Inside, the headstones lean at tired angles, and several graves are caged over with iron grilles, as if to keep something in rather than out. The lychgate is shut fast, its latch bound with knotted twine. The Dusty Road bends east past the graveyard wall and runs back south toward the gibbet.
rooms.2324: A stone cottage stands close by the road here, its shutters nailed fast and a crude sun daubed across its door in whitewash that has run in the rain. The garden before it is a tangle of nettles grown higher than the gate. Beyond its roof the dark woods have drawn much nearer. The road turns north past the cottage wall, and west it leads back toward the graveyard.
rooms.2325: Here the Dusty Road becomes a street, paved again with flags and lined by narrow houses of grey stone that share their walls. Every door is shut and every window shuttered, though a few window boxes still hold the dry brown stalks of geraniums, as if their owners meant to come back. A cast-iron pump stands at the kerb with its handle chained down. The street runs east between the houses and back south past the nailed cottage.
rooms.2326: The houses end at the foot of a steep, scrub-covered ridge, and the road divides. North, a branch of it plunges into the black mouth of a tunnel cut through the rock, its arch built of dressed stone and blotched with lichen. A cold draught breathes out of the dark. East, the main road runs toward a long, low building of tarred timber that straddles the way, and west lies the shuttered street.
rooms.2342: Daylight from the tunnel mouth to the south reaches a little way along the walls and then fails. The tunnel is broad enough for a wagon, its walls of fitted grey blocks sweating with damp, and old cart ruts run deep into the stone floor. Empty niches for lamps are set into the walls at intervals, black with the soot of flames long since gone out. The way runs on north into darkness.
rooms.2343: Deep inside the tunnel the darkness is almost complete, and every footstep comes back doubled from the curved roof. Water drips steadily from a crack overhead into a shallow pool worn in the floor. A refuge has been cut into one wall, a narrow alcove where a walker could press back to let a cart go by, and its stone bench is green with slime. The tunnel runs on north and back south toward the faint grey of daylight.
rooms.2344: The air stirs here, drawn along the tunnel by a draught from ahead that smells of wild grass and, faintly, of old ashes. The stone of the walls is streaked with long black scorch marks, as though a blast of fire had once roared through from the far end. The cart ruts stop short a few paces on, as if no wagon has gone further in living memory. A dim light shows to the north where the tunnel opens out, and southward the passage runs back into the dark.
rooms.2345: The tunnel ends in a high vaulted chamber, once a guardroom, where stone benches line the walls beneath arrow slits that let in thin blades of daylight. East, a massive gate of iron bars closes the way out into the Wild Valley, its lock rusted solid and its bars scorched black and warped, and words are cut deep into the lintel above it. Through the bars you glimpse green slopes and broken crags. The tunnel leads back south into darkness.
rooms.2327: A long tollhouse of tarred black timber straddles the road here, and the Dusty Road runs east into it through a pair of great doors propped open with stones. South, a narrow lane once led toward Town Line and Salem's Lot, but a gate of iron bars has been set across it and chained, and bunches of withered garlic hang from every crossbar. Brambles choke the lane beyond the bars. West, the road returns to the fork beneath the ridge.
rooms.2346: The road runs on beneath the roof of the tollhouse, a long gallery of tarred planks where daylight leaks in through the cracks in thin bright lines. A toll window with a rusted grille looks out from a booth on one side, and a board above it still lists the old charges in flaking paint. Straw and dust have drifted against the walls. The gallery runs on east into gloom, and back west to the great doors and the daylight.
rooms.2347: The tollhouse gallery comes to an end here, and the road meets a second pair of great doors set in the south wall. They are shut fast, barred with a beam of oak as thick as a man's waist and nailed across with planks, beyond which the road would run on to Town Line. Sun signs have been gouged into the wood with a knife, dozens of them, some crossed out and cut again. The gallery leads back west toward the daylight.
rooms.2310: A short path of scrubbed flagstones leads from the town square to the door of the largest house in the village, between low hedges of clipped box. A brass bell hangs from a bracket beside the door, its rope tied off neatly, for callers to announce themselves. A rowan tree shades the path, its berries scattered red across the stones. The square lies just north, and the elder's door opens to the west.
rooms.2311: The elder's house is a wide, low-beamed room that serves as both home and council chamber, with a long table and benches for a dozen neighbours at once. Over the hearth a sun is carved into the chimney breast and gilded, and beside it hangs a painted map of the parish, much handled. Shelves of ledgers and tithe rolls fill one wall, and the windows are fitted with iron bars on the inside. The door east leads out to the short path.
rooms.2308: A great wooden loom fills most of this one-roomed cottage, a half-finished length of blue cloth stretched across its frame. Baskets of carded wool are stacked by the hearth, and a spinning wheel waits beside a rocking chair worn pale on its arms. A line of salt has been poured along the sill of the only window, unbroken from end to end. The door opens north onto the Dusty Road.
rooms.8617: Beneath the golden trees the King's Road is crossed here by two lesser ways. South, the Path of Light slips off between a pair of ancient trunks whose leaves glow brighter than any around them, and a narrower arm of the road strikes off north. The broad paving itself runs on east toward the forest's edge and west deeper into the wood. A stone basin at the roadside holds rainwater that has caught the gold of the leaves above.
rooms.8618: This arm of the King's Road is older and narrower than the main way, its paving stones small, rounded and furred with moss along the joints. The golden trees still line it, but oaks have crept in among them, and their darker leaves make a patchwork of the light. A footpath leaves the road westward through a gap in the bracken. The road runs on north and back south to the crossing.
rooms.8619: The paving of the King's Road simply stops here, as though its builders laid one last stone and walked away. Beyond it a heap of dressed blocks, never set, has sunk into the moss beneath a great golden beech. A faint track, hardly more than a parting of the ferns, wanders off west among the trees and is soon lost to sight. The only clear way is back south along the road.
rooms.8649: It is easy to see how this path earned its name, for it fades in and out of the ferns and in places vanishes altogether beneath drifts of leaves. Old blazes cut into the bark of the trees have healed into faint scars, and someone has tied strips of faded red cloth to the branches to mark the way. East, the end of the paved road shows between the trunks, and west the path struggles on toward a broader trail.
rooms.8646: Four paths cross in a small clearing here, around a squat post of oak that bears an arrow carved for each of them, though the cuts have weathered almost smooth. Hornbeams with grey, twisted trunks ring the clearing, and woodpeckers have riddled a dead limb of one with neat round holes. The forest trail runs north toward the brighter trees and west along a mossy bank, a lesser path heads south, and a faint way wanders off east.
rooms.8648: The path bends here through a thicket of holly, its dark, glossy leaves so dense that the light beneath them is green and dim. Dead leaves crackle underfoot, and a mossy log lies along the edge of the way, hollowed by rot. Here and there a scarlet berry glows among the leaves. North, the path opens onto a clearing where trails cross, and east it winds on through the holly toward the King's Road.
rooms.8647: A forester's shelter stands beside the path here, a lean-to of poles roofed with bark and sods, with a ring of blackened stones before it where many fires have burned. The golden trees grow thickly again on this side of the holly, and their light falls warm across the trodden earth. The path forks: east to the old arm of the King's Road and south to the main road, while west it ducks back into the holly.
rooms.8615: A muddy track leaves the King's Road here, sliding off south between the golden trunks toward rough hill country, its ruts brimming with brown water. Beside it a weathered post bears a board with a single word, MARSHES, and a painted hand pointing the way with what looks like reluctance. North, a footpath enters the trees. The road itself runs west onto a stone bridge and on east beneath the shining leaves.
rooms.8616: The King's Road runs straight and level here, its pale stones swept clean and its verges trimmed back by the foresters' billhooks. A stone bench carved with a crown stands at the roadside for weary travellers, its seat dusted with fallen gold leaves. The leaves drift slowly even on windless days, turning over and over like spun coins. The road continues east toward a crossing and west toward a bridge.
rooms.8704: Leaving the golden trees behind, the path runs out into open hill country and turns at once to mud, a sticky brown slough that sucks at every step. Rough grass and tussocks cover the slopes on either hand, and the wind blows cold after the shelter of the forest. Far ahead, beyond the folded hills, bare grey crags rise into a haze that never seems to lift. North, the trees of the King's Road glow at the top of the slope, and the path squelches on south.
rooms.8705: A cart has been abandoned here, sunk to its axles in the mire with one wheel snapped and its shafts pointing at the sky. Whoever owned it took the horse and left the rest to rot, and grass now grows from the boards of its bed. The wind hums through the gorse. The path bends around the wreck through heather, climbing north toward the forest and running on south over the shoulder of the hill.
rooms.8706: A cairn of grey stones marks a parting of the ways on the hillside, its top stone daubed with a red warning mark. East, a stony track climbs toward the crags, where a pale mist lies over the Dead Marshes and a smell of stagnant water drifts on the wind. No sheep graze here, and the grass grows long and rank around the cairn. The muddy path itself winds on south between the hills, and north it climbs back toward the forest.
rooms.8736: The Dead Marshes lie in a high bowl among the crags, a maze of black pools and sodden moss threaded between ribs of bare grey rock. Nothing green grows here; the reeds are brown and broken, and the water is so still it holds the sky like dark glass. The cold bites deeper than the height alone can explain. A stony gully leads south off the rock toward the lower path, the track from the cairn returns west, and the marsh stretches on east.
rooms.8737: A crag of bare rock rears over the marsh here, its face streaked white where water seeps from the cracks. Below it a long black mere lies edged with rotting reeds, and a line of flat stones, set by some forgotten hand, picks across the bog. Beneath the still water pale shapes seem to drift and turn, though they are gone whenever you look straight at them. The stones lead north and west through the marsh, and a scree slope falls away south toward the muddy path.
rooms.8738: The marsh ends against a sheer wall of dark rock, and the last of the bog lies in its shadow, where old grey snow survives in the crevices long after the thaw. A ring of standing stones rises from the black water, half drowned and leaning, their tops crusted with pale lichen. The air is utterly still and very cold. The only way out is back south across the stepping stones.
rooms.8709: Loose scree has spilled across the path here from the crags above, and the mud between the stones is the colour of rust. A thin spring trickles out of the hillside into a pool ringed with cress, the only clean water for some distance. Hoofprints of deer are pressed into the soft ground around it. The path turns at the spring, running west along the slope and south between two rounded hills.
rooms.8710: The muddy path comes to an end in a hollow between the hills, where a firmer track of beaten earth strikes off east toward a dark line of trees. An old turf dyke runs across the hollow, breached where the paths meet, and heather grows thick along its top. After so much mud the hard ground is a relief underfoot. North, the mire leads back toward the spring.
rooms.8711: The track passes through a belt of old pines that cap the hill, their trunks red-barked and straight and their crowns sighing in the wind. Needles lie deep and dry underfoot, and the air is sharp with resin. Old axe-cuts scar a few of the trunks, long since healed over with gum. The path turns here, running south out of the pines along a ridge and west back to the hollow where the muddy path ends.
rooms.8712: The path runs along the spine of a ridge here, open to every wind, with the land falling away in long slopes of heather and bilberry on either side. Ahead, beyond the hills, a vast dark sea of treetops stretches to the horizon. Clouds race low overhead, trailing their shadows across the slopes. North, a stand of pines crowns the next rise, and southward the path keeps to the ridge.
rooms.8713: A lone hawthorn grows beside the path on this windswept stretch of ridge, bent so far by the gales that its crown nearly brushes the ground. In its lee stand the tumbled walls of a shepherd's bothy, roofless now, its hearthstone still black with old fires. Tufts of wool snagged on the thorns flutter like small grey flags. The path follows the ridge north and south through the heather.
rooms.8714: The ridge ends at a knoll of weathered grey rock, split by frost into great blocks that lean against one another like tired giants. The path skirts around them and turns west, slanting off the high ground through bracken toward the edge of the dark forest. From here the country of hills lies spread out behind you like a rumpled blanket. North, the path runs back along the windy spine of the ridge.
rooms.8715: At the foot of the hills the path reaches the edge of the Old Forest, where enormous trees stand shoulder to shoulder like a wall. Two moss-grown gateposts mark where a small road once began, and it runs on south between them into the shadow beneath the boughs. East, the path climbs back through the bracken toward the ridge. The air from the forest is cool and smells of leaf mould.
rooms.8716: A small road runs beneath the Old Forest here, so old that only its kerbstones still show, two lines of mossy blocks with a carpet of leaf mould between them. Huge oaks lean over it, their limbs bearded with ivy, and the light beneath them is a deep green dusk even at noon. North, daylight glimmers where the road leaves the trees for the hills, and south it runs on into the gloom.
rooms.8717: The small road bends east here, but something has torn a great gap in the forest to the south, as though a giant had walked through the trees and snapped them at the knee. Shattered trunks lie in a long swathe, all pointing the same way, their splintered ends blackened by fire. Young birches have sprouted among them. North, the road runs back toward the hills.
rooms.8719: The road crosses a brown, slow brook here on a single arch of stone so overgrown with moss and fern that it looks more like a natural bank than anything built. The water slides beneath without a sound, and the trees crowd so close on either side that their roots dip into it. Long strands of weed stream in the current like green hair. The road runs on east into deeper shade and west toward the bend.
rooms.8720: An immense hollow oak stands at this turn of the road, its trunk split open into a dark cleft wide enough to step inside, though nothing about it invites you to. Thick grey webs are strung across the cleft and between the lower branches, sagging with old dead leaves. The road turns south here, and west it runs back toward the mossy bridge. The forest is very quiet.
rooms.8721: Roots as thick as a man's body have pushed through the road here, heaving its old stones into humps and hollows that make every step a scramble. Bracket fungus, orange and cream, climbs the nearest trunks in shelves. Somewhere overhead a branch creaks, though no wind reaches the ground. The road turns east, and north it leads back toward the hollow oak.
rooms.8722: A forest giant has fallen beside the road here, and its upturned roots stand taller than a house, still clutching boulders in their grip. The hole it tore in the canopy lets a single broad shaft of sunlight fall onto the stones, and foxgloves crowd into the light, tall and purple against the green. The road turns south past the roots, and west it leads back over the heaved stones.
rooms.8723: Ancient yews close in on both sides of the road here, their trunks fluted and twisted and their dark foliage shutting out nearly all the light. Long ago someone carved a face into the bark of the largest, and the tree has grown around it so that the face seems to peer out from deep inside the wood. The road runs on north toward a patch of sunlight and south through the yews.
rooms.8724: The trees begin to thin here, and a grey brightness shows between the trunks ahead where the forest comes to an end. The road's old paving reappears from under the leaf mould, cracked and tilted but still in its lines, and brambles reach across it from both sides. Blackberries hang heavy on them, though none have been picked. South lies the forest's edge, and north the road plunges back among the yews.
rooms.8725: The Old Forest ends abruptly at the lip of a steep escarpment, and so does the road, its last stones hanging broken over a raw scar where the hillside has slipped away. Far below and beyond, a wide country of misty fields and distant woods stretches away under an open sky. There is no way across the landslip. The road leads back north into the shadow of the trees.
rooms.8718: At the end of the swathe of broken trees lies a wide crater, its sides furred with young birch and its floor strangely bare. In the middle sits the meteorite, a great lump of black, pitted stone half buried in the earth, with a metallic sheen where the rain has washed it. The ground around it has run and hardened like glass, and the air smells faintly of hot iron. The only way out is north through the fallen trees.
rooms.8708: Peat has been cut from the hillside here, leaving black terraced banks above the path and a few stacks of turves drying under a heap of stones. The diggers have not been back in some time, and water has pooled in the cuttings, brown as strong tea. High above, grey crags hide whatever lies beyond them. The muddy path runs on east along the slope and west around the flank of the hill.
rooms.8707: The path fords a peaty stream here on a line of stepping stones, each one slick with brown slime and set just a little too far from the next. Beyond the ford the mud is churned deep, and the path bends east around the foot of a heather-clad hill. The stream chatters over the stones, the only cheerful sound for miles. North, the path climbs toward the cairn at the parting of the ways.
rooms.8614: The King's Road crosses a deep, rocky stream here on a bridge of a single high arch, built of the same pale stone as the road and wide enough for two wagons to pass. Golden trees lean out over the water from both banks, and their fallen leaves ride the current below like flecks of gilt. A crowned shield is carved on the keystone of each parapet. The road runs on east and west among the trees.
rooms.8613: Just short of the bridge, the bank beside the King's Road falls away steeply toward the stream, and a small rocky path leads down from the roadside, zigzagging between boulders and hazel toward a wooded hollow below. Ferns spill over the edge of the paving. The trees in the hollow are a plain, sober green, untouched by the gold that lines the road. The road runs east onto the bridge and west deeper into the golden wood.
rooms.8612: A trail crosses the King's Road here, and the two halves of it could hardly be less alike. North it wanders off cheerfully into a wood of oak and gold, while south it plunges into a wall of dark, close-grown trees where the light dies within a few paces: the Trail of Shadows. A post at its mouth bears a board painted with the foresters' crown and a single word, WARE. The road runs on east toward a bridge and west beneath the golden boughs.
rooms.8628: The trail leaves the King's Road behind and winds north between oaks and golden ash trees, its earth packed hard by the boots of foresters. A neat stack of cut logs stands beside it, roofed with bark and waiting to be carted away, and sawdust still lies pale on the ground around it. A side trail branches west through the bracken, and south the paving of the road shows bright between the trunks.
rooms.8629: Beneath a great old oak at this fork, the earth has been dug into a sprawling badger sett, its spoil heaps of yellow sand scattered with old bedding and scraps of bone. One entrance is wide enough for a person to crawl down into, a dark mouth between two roots. The trail runs on north as a narrower animal track, and east a path heads off toward the sound of rushing water. South, the trail returns toward the King's Road.
rooms.8639: The path runs along the very rim of the ravine here, so close to the edge that someone has driven iron pegs into the rock and strung a rope between them as a rail. Far below, the stream boils white through a chute of black stone. Hart's-tongue ferns sprout from every crack, and the air is damp with spray. The rim path runs north toward a bridge and south along the gorge, and a trail leads west into the trees.
rooms.8638: The ravine path ends at a jutting shelf of rock, where the stream leaps out over a lip of stone and falls in a long white plume into a deep green pool far below. A seat has been cut into the rock at the edge of the shelf, worn smooth by those who come to watch. Mist rises from the falls and beads every leaf with water. The only way on is back north along the rim.
rooms.8627: The trail passes through an old charcoal burners' clearing, where a wide ring of earth is still black and nothing grows but a few thin grasses. A turf hut has slumped into a low green mound at its edge. The smell of old smoke lingers in the soil after rain. North, an animal path slips away into the bracken, east the trail runs on among the oaks, and south it leads to the King's Road.
rooms.8626: This is a deer track rather than a path, a narrow groove through head-high bracken that closes behind you as you pass. Slots of cloven hooves are pressed into every soft patch, and tufts of reddish hair cling to a low branch where something rubbed past. The fronds leave your clothes dusted with brown spores. The track runs north toward a trampled clearing, west through the bracken, and south to a wider trail.
rooms.8623: The animal path skirts a grey beech whose trunk has been shredded in long, parallel furrows, the torn bark hanging in strips and the pale wood beneath still weeping sap. The ground at its foot is torn open and strewn with rotten wood where something dug for grubs. A musky, animal smell hangs in the air. North, the path meets an old overgrown road; east and south it wanders on through the undergrowth.
rooms.8622: The animal path drops into a ditch at the edge of the King's Road and climbs out again over a fallen log, worn smooth on top by the passage of many hooves and paws. Golden leaves from the roadside trees drift into the bracken here. A small path, neater than the game trail, leads off west, and the animal path wanders north into the wood. South lies the road.
rooms.8609: The King's Road turns here at a bend shaded by a vast golden lime, its heart-shaped leaves glowing like lamps. Set into a niche in the roadside bank is a little shrine of carved stone, a stag with a sun between its antlers, hung about with faded ribbons. The air beneath the lime is sweet and drowsy. The road runs on east and south, and a deer track slips away north into the bracken.
rooms.8610: The paving dips through a shallow hollow here, where a spring wells up beside the road and is led away beneath it through a stone culvert. Moss grows thick and bright around the spring, studded with tiny white flowers, and the golden trees above lean together into an arch. The water is clear and very cold. The King's Road runs on east and climbs gently west toward a bend.
rooms.8611: A milestone capped with a carved crown stands at the roadside here, its face giving the leagues back to Garathorm in letters picked out in faded red. On one side of the road the golden trees stand tall and bright, but on the other their gold gives way within a stone's throw to the dark, crowding trees of an older wood. The road runs on east toward a crossing and west into a hollow.
rooms.8608: The King's Road runs north and south here along the edge of a darker wood, and the golden trees grow thin and pale on its eastern side. East, a narrow way slips off between black trunks into the gloom of the Trail of Shadows, and even at midday the air that breathes out of it is cold. An iron bracket on a post holds a lantern cage, empty and rusted, as if someone once thought a light here worth the trouble.
rooms.8696: Under the first black trees of the Trail of Shadows the gold of the King's Road seems a world away, though its paving still glimmers both north and west between the trunks. The trees here are dark-barked and close, their branches knitted into a roof that lets through only a grey, sourceless light. Sounds carry oddly, and your own footsteps seem to come a moment late. East, the tangled Old Forest presses in, and south the trail runs on into deeper shadow.
rooms.8733: The Old Forest closes in at once, a press of ancient, lichen-grey trunks that seem to stand a little nearer each time you look away. A path of sorts leads north between them, but it twists among the roots and somehow returns you to where you began. Dead leaves lie ankle-deep, and nothing stirs in them. South, the trees open a gap into deeper forest, and west lies the dim Trail of Shadows.
rooms.8734: Paths fork and fork again in this part of the Old Forest, and the ways north and east, though they set off in different directions, soon wind together among the same grey trunks. A dead elm stands in the midst of them, white and barkless, its bare limbs spread like a signpost that has forgotten its words. South, the forest grows darker still, and west the Trail of Shadows passes close by.
rooms.8735: Grey willows of enormous age begin to crowd among the other trees here, their trunks split and hollow and their long leaves hissing softly though the air is still. The ground is soft and black, and roots loop out of it like the ribs of buried things. It is hard to shake the feeling that the willows are listening. A narrow way threads north between the trunks and south toward damper ground.
rooms.8699: A great boulder lies among the trees here, split cleanly in two as if by a single blow, and an oak sapling grows from the crack between the halves. Strangely, no moss or lichen clings to its sides, though every other stone in the Old Forest is furred with green. Ways lead north among the willows and south toward the smell of water, and westward the dark Trail of Shadows runs close by.
rooms.8701: The ground grows wetter here, and the forest floor gives way to beds of royal fern and sphagnum that quake underfoot. A low mist hangs between the alders, never rising above knee height, and the trunks seem to stand in milk. Every sound is muffled, as if the mist swallows it. The firmest way follows a ridge of roots north toward drier ground and south toward the gleam of open water.
rooms.8702: Through a screen of alders the dark water of a lake shines east, and a trodden way slants toward it between the roots. The trees here lean out toward the light, their trunks bent and their bark scabbed with grey lichen. Someone long ago carved initials into a fallen trunk beside the way, a pair of letters inside a heart, now swollen and blurred. North, the forest closes again in mist.
rooms.8703: The trees give way to a narrow shore of grey shingle at the edge of a still forest lake, its water so dark that it looks bottomless. Lily pads float in the shallows, and dead reeds rattle in the breeze. Out on the lake a small wooded island rises, crowned by a green mound, and a causeway of tumbled stones runs east toward it. West, the Old Forest waits behind the alders.
rooms.8726: The causeway runs out across the middle of the lake here, a spine of flat stones barely a stride wide, with black water lapping at its edges on either hand. Some of the stones have sunk, and you must step from one to the next over cold, clear shallows where weed waves far below. Mist smokes off the water in thin, curling wisps. South, the causeway turns toward the little island and its mound, and west it leads back to the shingle shore.
rooms.8727: The small island is little more than a grassy hump in the lake, ringed with twisted thorn trees and crowned by an ancient barrow mound. Weathered standing stones circle the mound, and on its near side a dark doorway framed by three great slabs opens onto a stair of worn steps that leads down into the earth. No sound reaches the island from the forest. North, the stepping-stone causeway leads back across the water.
rooms.8676: Strings of small bones, feathers and knotted hair hang from the low branches over the trail here, turning slowly though the air hangs dead and still. Whoever hung them meant them as a warning, or a ward, and they click softly against each other in the gloom. The trail beneath them is bare earth, as though few care to linger. The trail runs on north and south, and a gap in the trees opens east into the Old Forest.
rooms.8675: The trail skirts a sunken pool of black water here, its surface skinned with a film like oil and its banks bare of any growing thing. The white bones of a horse lie half in and half out of the water, picked clean long ago. No reflection shows in the pool, not even of the branches overhead. North and south the trail runs on beneath the dark trees, and west the roots of the Old Forest reach out across the path.
rooms.8698: The trail sinks into a deep cutting here, its banks so high and so overhung with roots that it runs like a tunnel through the earth. Water drips from the roots onto the path, and the walls of the cutting are slick with black mud. Crow feathers, black and glossy, are stuck in the mud at the foot of the banks. A gap in the bank to the east lets in a little grey light from the Old Forest, and the sunken trail runs on north and south.
rooms.8697: The burnt shell of a wagon lies on its side beside the trail here, its canvas long gone and its ribs charred black. Nobody has salvaged its wheels or iron, which says something about how little anyone cares to linger on the Trail of Shadows. The trail runs north toward the King's Road and south into deeper gloom, and to the east the tangle of the Old Forest begins.
rooms.8674: Two fallen trunks lean together over the way here like the rafters of a roofless house, and ferns sprout thickly from the rot along their backs. Beneath them the light is the colour of weak tea. Beetles have carved twisting galleries in the bare wood where the bark has fallen away. The Old Forest presses close on every side, but a way leads east toward the Trail of Shadows and west into deeper wood.
rooms.8673: This is the deep heart of the Old Forest, where every way looks the same and the trees seem to have been placed to confuse. Grey trunks march off in endless ranks, their crowns woven so tightly together that sun and sky are only guesses. Many a traveller has strayed in here from the paths and wandered in circles for days. A way of sorts leads north, and another east toward the Trail of Shadows.
rooms.8672: A stream has cut a deep, narrow bed through the forest floor here, and the way crosses it on a fallen trunk furred with moss. The water is black, quick and strangely silent, and pale roots trail into it like fingers. Water drips from every leaf long after the rain has stopped. Paths of a sort lead north toward the King's Road, east among dense hollies, and south into the confusing depths of the wood.
rooms.8671: Just beyond the verge of the King's Road the Old Forest begins in earnest, and the gold of the roadside trees can still be glimpsed through the branches to the north. A vast thicket of blackthorn blocks the way ahead, and paths skirt it east and west, though both wind around it to the same hidden glade. The thorns are hung with tufts of fur and scraps of cloth. Another way leads south between grey trunks.
rooms.8607: The King's Road turns north here at a sharp bend, banked with pale stone where the wheels of heavy wagons have swung wide over the years. On the outer side of the bend the golden trees end at a ditch, and beyond it the dark ranks of the Old Forest begin, with a gap in the ditch letting a path slip off south among them. West, the road runs straight back through the shining wood.
rooms.8606: A forester's lodge stands back from the road here in a clearing of its own, a snug house of golden-brown logs with a crown carved over its door and antlers nailed to its gable. Its shutters are closed and its door is locked, though a thread of smoke sometimes rises from the chimney. A rain barrel and a chopping block stand by the porch. The King's Road runs on east toward a bend and west between the shining trees.
rooms.8605: Dozens of little cairns of pebbles line the verge along this stretch of the King's Road, each built by some traveller in thanks for a safe passage through the forest. Golden leaves have drifted against them and half buried the smallest. The trees here are very old and very tall, their pale trunks rising straight as columns. The road runs on east and west through their light.
rooms.8604: The stump of an old stone watchtower stands beside the road here, ivy-clad and roofless, its stair long since fallen so that no one can climb it. Golden saplings have taken root in its empty windows, and their leaves shine out of the grey stone like candle flames. Crowns and initials have been scratched into the stones at its base. The King's Road runs past its foot, east past a row of little cairns and west through the trees.
rooms.8603: The trees stand back from the road here around a wide glade of short grass starred with yellow flowers. Light pools in it like water in a bowl, and the foresters say that even on moonless nights a soft gold glow lingers here long after sunset. A single golden oak grows in the middle of the glade, its lowest boughs sweeping the grass. The King's Road crosses the glade east to west.
rooms.8602: A barrier pole painted in bands of red and white stands raised on its post beside the road here, where the king's foresters can lower it to stop wagons if they choose. A little sentry box of planks stands beside it, and a board nailed to its side forbids fires, felling and hunting in the royal wood without warrant. The golden trees grow thicker going east, and west the light of open country shows at the forest's edge.
rooms.8601: Here the King's Road leaves open grassland and passes between two enormous golden trees that stand on either side of it like gateposts, their roots heaving the first paving stones of the forest road. Beyond them the wood glows, every leaf holding the light as if reluctant to let it go. East, the road runs on beneath the shining canopy, and west it leads out into open country toward a crossing and the castle town's wall.
rooms.8728: Behind the blackthorn lies a hidden glade, where the stump of some unimaginably old tree spreads as wide as a cottage floor, its rings too many to count. Moss and pale toadstools have colonised its rotten heart. Whatever felled it left no trace of axe or saw. Paths leave the glade east and south between grey trunks, and west a way winds back around the thorns toward the King's Road.
rooms.8729: Webs as broad as sails are strung between the firs here, grey and heavy with dew, and some are so thick that they blot out what little light there is. Bundles wrapped in old silk hang among them, shrivelled and still, and it is better not to wonder what they once were. A path ducks beneath the lowest strands, running west toward the glade and south into deeper gloom.
rooms.8732: A trapper's hut once stood in this hollow, but only its chimney of piled stones still stands upright, the rest a heap of rotten logs smothered in bramble. A rusted iron hook juts from the chimney breast where a kettle once hung. Whoever lived here left in a hurry, or did not leave at all. Faint paths lead north toward the webbed firs, south into a tangle of holly, and west between the grey trunks.
rooms.8730: Holly grows so densely here that the forest becomes a maze of dark, prickling walls, and the light that filters through is green and cold. A gap to the west looks promising, but it winds through the thicket in a tight circle and delivers you back to this same patch of leaf mould. Boot prints going round and round in the soft ground show that others have been fooled before. North, a clearer way leads back toward the ruined hut.
rooms.8731: An old pitfall gapes beside the way here, a square shaft dug by hunters long ago, its rotten cover of branches collapsed into it. Sharpened stakes, grey and soft with age, still bristle from the leaves that fill its bottom. It would be easy to blunder into it in the gloom. The way edges past it, leading north toward the glade with the great stump, east toward the ruined hut and west to the stream.
rooms.8677: Low cairns of grey stones line both sides of the trail here, each the length of a man, and some have a stick or a broken blade thrust into the top as a marker. These are the graves of travellers who did not finish the Trail of Shadows, buried by those who did. Several of the cairns have been disturbed, their stones scattered. The trail runs north between the dark trees and south toward older, stranger country.
rooms.8678: The trail bends west here around a fallen pillar of white stone, the first sign of the ancient city that once stood somewhere in this forest. The pillar is fluted and finely carved, but the trees have grown over and around it, and roots grip it like a fist. The shadows beneath the trees seem deeper here than the leaves can account for. North, the trail leads back past the travellers' graves.
rooms.8679: Under the leaf litter the trail here runs on great flagstones of the same white stone, the paving of some forgotten road. A carved head, as large as a cartwheel and with its nose broken away, lies on its side among the ferns, gazing at nothing. East the trail leads back to the fallen pillar, south it follows the old paving deeper into shadow, and north a faint way pushes into the Old Forest.
rooms.8680: Every tree in this stretch of the forest is dead, grey and leafless, yet none has fallen, and they stand in their ranks like an army turned to stone. Without leaves they should let in the light, but the sky above them is a dull, sunless grey, and the shadows lie thick on the old paving. The trail turns east here, and north it leads back past the carved head.
rooms.8681: Low walls of white stone begin to show among the trees here, the foundations of houses swallowed long ago by the forest, their doorways choked with nettles. A broken archway leans over the trail, its keystone gone, yet somehow it still stands. Somewhere ahead water drips into stone with a slow, hollow note. The trail turns south toward the heart of the ruins, and west it runs back among the dead trees.
rooms.8682: The Trail of Shadows ends before the gate of a ruined city, where two broken towers of white stone flank the old road, their tops snapped off and crowned with ferns. The gate between them is long gone, and the road passes south through the gap into a wilderness of fallen walls and black trees. Huge iron hinge-pins still jut from the towers, rusted into red stumps. North, the trail leads back among the foundations.
rooms.8683: Inside the broken gate a wide street of white flagstones opens out, heaved and split by the black trees that grow straight through it. Shells of houses line it, roofless and hollow-eyed, their upper floors long since fallen into their cellars. The silence is so complete that your footsteps sound like trespass. Streets lead east and west through the ruins, and north the gap between the towers leads back out to the trail.
rooms.8684: A colonnade of white columns runs along this street, a dozen still standing in a row and holding nothing but the sky. Behind them the floor of some great hall lies open to the weather, its mosaic of black and white tiles buckled by roots. Here and there the mosaic still shows part of a picture: a hand, a wing, a crowned head. The street turns south past the columns, and west it leads back toward the gate.
rooms.8685: A great fountain basin of cracked marble stands in the middle of the street here, empty but for drifted leaves and a black puddle of rainwater. West, through a gap in the fallen walls, a broad open space can be seen, and at its far side the dark bulk of a building that seems to have resisted the forest better than the rest. The street runs north toward the colonnade and south deeper into the ruins.
rooms.8686: This narrow lane winds between the ruins of tall houses, whose walls still stand two storeys high in places, pierced by empty windows. A stone stair climbs the outside of one house and ends abruptly in empty air where the upper floor used to be. Ivy hangs in curtains over everything. The lane runs north to the fountain and west between the walls.
rooms.8687: A toppled statue lies across this crossing of ruined streets, a robed figure twice the height of a man, broken into three pieces at the waist and knees. Its upturned face has been worn featureless by rain. In one stone hand it still clutches the stub of a key. North, the streets open into a great square at the centre of the ruins, while lanes run east and west between crumbling walls.
rooms.8688: The streets of the ruined city meet in a great round square paved in rings of black and white stone, with a dead tree standing at its very centre. North rises a squat, windowless temple of black rock that guards the entrance to the Undertombs, but its doorway is sealed by an iron grate set deep in the stone, the lock rusted into a single lump. Cold air breathes through the bars from the darkness beyond. Streets leave the square east, south and west.
rooms.8690: An old well stands in this small paved court, its round stone head carved with a band of leaves and its windlass long since rotted away. Iron rungs set into the shaft lead down into darkness, slick with moss but still sound. From far below comes the faint, hollow sound of dripping water. The great square lies east, and lanes lead north and south between the ruined walls.
rooms.8689: A corner of the old city wall stands here, still sound enough to hold the remains of a painted fresco on its inner face: a feast in a garden of golden trees, the dancers faded almost to ghosts. Black trees have rooted along the foot of the wall. Rain has washed the faces from every one of the dancers. A street runs east toward the gate, and a lane leads south toward a court with a well.
rooms.8691: The ruins thin out here against the remains of the city's outer wall, which has been breached by a great tree whose trunk now fills the gap like a cork. Beside it a small postern gate still stands, its door gone, and a narrow trail slips out through it to the south. Moss has turned the stones of the wall a deep, velvety green. Lanes run north toward the well and east toward the toppled statue.
rooms.8692: The narrow trail squeezes between walls of bramble and blackthorn, so tight in places that the thorns snag at every step. Behind, the white stones of the ruined city gleam among the black trees, and ahead the gloom begins to lift, with real daylight showing between the trunks. The air smells of crushed leaves and, faintly, of open fields. The trail runs north back through the postern and south toward the edge of the forest.
rooms.8693: The trees end here at the brow of a long slope, and beyond them open country rolls away under a wide, pale sky, fields and far-off hills hazy with distance. A trail seems to lead on south across the slope, yet every time it is followed it curls back through a fringe of birches to this same spot, as though the forest is unwilling to let anyone leave this way. North, the narrow trail returns toward the ruins.
rooms.8600: The small path ends in a sunny dell where someone once kept a garden, fenced with woven hazel hurdles that have half collapsed. Rosemary, sage and thyme have run wild and spread far beyond the hurdles, and the warm air is heavy with their scent. A flat stone serves as a seat beside a tiny spring. The only way out is east, back to the animal path.
rooms.8645: The forest trail follows the foot of a long, mossy bank here, where beech roots twist out of the earth like the coils of great grey serpents. A trickle of water seeps from the bank and keeps the path soft and dark. Primroses grow in the damp along its foot. North, the trail climbs toward a fork among the chestnuts, and east it runs on to a small clearing where four paths cross.
rooms.8650: The Path of Light begins between two ancient golden trees whose boughs meet overhead in an arch, and passing beneath them is like stepping into a warm room. A narrow way of white pebbles runs on south, edged with moss, and the leaves above glow so brightly that the path seems lit from within. Even the air tastes faintly of honey. North, the King's Road lies just beyond the arch.
rooms.8651: The pebbled path runs straight between slender golden trees, their bark pale as birch and their leaves stirring and whispering of their own accord. Shafts of light fall across the way at the same low slant whatever the hour, so that morning and evening look much alike here. A small stone marker carved with a sun stands at the path's edge. The path runs on north and south.
rooms.8652: The path turns east beside a still, round pool whose water mirrors the golden canopy so perfectly that it seems to hold a second forest beneath its surface. Flat stones have been set around its rim for sitting, and their tops are worn smooth. Fallen leaves float on the water without sinking, slowly turning. North, the pebbled path leads back toward the King's Road.
rooms.8653: Here the golden trees grow close on either side, their trunks wrapped in a pale, silvery bark that seems to give off a faint light of its own. The white pebbles of the path are swept clean, though no one is ever seen sweeping them. Tiny gold flowers, no bigger than a fingernail, grow in the moss along the edges. The path runs east toward a crossing and west to the still pool.
rooms.8654: Four ways meet at the heart of the Path of Light, around a standing stone of yellow crystal taller than a man. Light gathers inside the stone and glows there softly, brightening when clouds pass over as if to make up for the hidden sun. A small trail slips away north between the trees, the pebbled path runs east and west, and another branch of it leads south beneath the golden boughs.
rooms.8655: The small trail winds away from the crystal stone and ends in a tiny glade, hardly bigger than a room, walled in by golden saplings. A bower has been woven from living branches at its far side, the stems bent and tied until they have grown into a leafy roof over a seat of moss. It is very quiet here, and the light is soft and green-gold. The only way back is south.
rooms.8656: The path bends south here around a golden tree so old that its trunk has split into three, each part as thick as an ordinary oak, the three leaning apart like dancers. Its fallen leaves lie heaped against the roots in a glittering drift that crunches softly underfoot. The pebbles run west toward the crystal stone and south deeper into the radiant wood.
rooms.8658: Another crossing of pale paths opens here within a ring of golden trees planted at even spaces, like the pillars of a round hall with the sky for its roof. The ground inside the ring is carpeted with short, fine grass that never seems to need cutting. Ways lead north and west among the trees, east toward a brighter glow, and south along the pebbled path.
rooms.8659: The path ends in the brightest place in all the forest, a sunken glade where the light lies so thick and golden that it is like wading through warm water. Nothing casts a shadow here, not even you. A spring rises in the middle of the glade and spills over a lip of white stone into a pebbled runnel. The only way out is west, back to the ring of trees.
rooms.8661: The pebbled path runs east and west here along the foot of a gentle bank covered in golden moss, and a branch of it climbs north toward the ring of trees. Ferns of a pale yellow-green unfurl along the bank, and the air is warm and still. A stone trough set into the bank catches the water of a little rill and lets it overflow into the moss. Its trickle is the only sound.
rooms.8662: The golden trees thin a little here, and between their trunks you catch the first glimpses of darker woods somewhere beyond, grey and brooding against the glow. The path runs on east and west between low banks of moss, its white pebbles fewer now and sunk deep into the earth. A wooden bench, silvered with age, has been set where travellers can rest and look back at the light.
rooms.8663: The path turns south here, and the gold of the forest begins to fade, the leaves overhead paler and fewer and the light a thinner yellow. A carved post stands at the corner, a sun at its top and beneath it a crescent moon turned on its back like a cradle. South, the path heads toward the edge of the bright wood, and west it returns among the shining trees.
rooms.8664: Here the Path of Light comes to its end, the last golden trees standing in a line like a guard of honour on either side of the pebbles. Beyond them a narrower trail runs on south through a lighter wood of slim birch and aspen, and on both sides of it the dark Old Forest crowds close. The glow of the radiant trees lies at your back to the north. The air grows cooler with every step.
rooms.1301: A trail runs south through a light, airy wood of silver birches, their white trunks bright against the gloom of the Old Forest that stands close on either hand. Step off the trail east or west and you would be among the dark trunks at once, and easily lost. Birch leaves flicker and turn in the faintest breath of air. North, the golden trees mark the end of the Path of Light.
rooms.1302: Aspens grow among the birches here, their round leaves trembling and chattering with every stir of wind. The trail is a ribbon of short grass and fallen leaves, easy to follow, but the Old Forest looms only a few paces away east and west, its shadows reaching across the path. Ferns grow tall along the verges. The trail runs on north and south between the pale trunks.
rooms.1303: A fallen birch lies along the edge of the trail here, its white bark peeling in papery curls and its wood gone soft and orange with rot. Beyond it, east and west, the dark ranks of the Old Forest wait, and paths of a sort lead into them, worn by those who strayed. The light trail itself continues north and south, bright and narrow, between the pale trees.
rooms.1304: The trail turns west here, swerving around a dense knot of holly beyond which, south and east alike, the Old Forest begins at once, black and close. Faint ways lead into it, but they would soon have you wandering in circles. Bracken grows thick at the bend, bronzed at its tips. North, the trail runs back between the birches.
rooms.1305: The trail bends again here, coming in from the east and turning south, and the pale wood narrows to a strip only a few trees wide. The Old Forest presses close to the north and west, so close that its roots creep across the grass of the trail. A young rowan, bright with berries, grows at the corner as if to mark the way. Lichen hangs in grey beards from the nearest dark branches.
rooms.1306: The light wood widens a little here into a long, narrow glade of grass and harebells, sunlit and quiet. On either side, east and west, the edge of the Old Forest is as sharp as a wall, dark trunks standing shoulder to shoulder just beyond the last of the birches. The trail runs straight through the glade, north and south.
rooms.1307: A little stream crosses the trail here, shallow and clear over a bed of pale pebbles, and someone has laid a pair of flat stones in it for stepping across. The water comes out of the Old Forest on one side and vanishes into it on the other, and dark paths follow it both east and west into the gloom. The trail goes on north and south among the slim white trees.
rooms.1308: The birches here are hung with the first golden leaves again, a few at first and then more, as the trail nears the edge of the Radiant Forest to the south. The Old Forest still hems the trail east and west, but its gloom seems to shrink back from the brightening trees. North, the pale trail runs on through the birch wood.
rooms.1311: The birch trail ends at the bright margin of the Radiant Forest, where golden boughs arch overhead and the light thickens into a warm glow. The edge of the wood runs east and west, gold on one hand and the brooding Old Forest on the other, and south a path leads on beneath the shining trees toward a scent of honeysuckle. North, the pale birch trail runs back toward the Path of Light.
rooms.1312: Along this stretch of the margin the golden trees stand in a long, unbroken line, and their roots and those of the Old Forest wrestle together in the moss beneath. North, the dark wood begins at once, its shadows lying across the grass like spilled ink. The bright edge runs east toward a corner and west toward the end of the birch trail.
rooms.1313: The Radiant Forest turns a corner here, its golden margin bending away south while the Old Forest wraps around it to the north and east like a dark cloak. A white stone, smooth and round as an egg, has been set into the moss at the very corner, the first of a line that runs on south along the edge. West, the bright margin leads back toward the birch trail.

2321.description: Most of the lettering has been hacked away, but the deep-cut numeral II survives, and beneath it the ghost of an S and an L. The chisel scars are old and weathered smooth, as though someone long ago wished travellers not to know how near Salem's Lot lay.

2345.description: Letters a hand high are cut into the stone above the gate: THE VALLEY IS NOT YOURS. Beneath them, scratched much smaller and in haste, someone has added: NOR OURS.

2346.description: The flaking list reads: A CART, TWO PENCE. HORSE AND RIDER, ONE PENNY. SHEEP AND SWINE, BY THE SCORE. At the bottom a later hand has added in red paint: NONE AFTER DARK, AT ANY PRICE.

2311.description: The map shows the village, its fields and the Dusty Road winding away past the heath. Where the road runs on toward Salem's Lot the paint has been rubbed thin by many fingers, and a careful hand has lettered in the margin: GO BY DAY, AND COME HOME BY DAY.

8738.description: The stones are carved with rows of small figures linked hand to hand, walking into water that the carver drew as wavy lines. Whatever the figures were walking toward has been worn away, or deliberately broken off.

8718.description: The stone is warm to the touch even on cold days, and a faint hum seems to come from somewhere deep inside it. Chisel marks around its base show where someone tried to chip a piece away, and the broken tip of the chisel is still lodged in it, fused to the metal.

8723.description: The face is bearded with leaves and its mouth hangs open, as if speaking or singing. The bark has swollen around the eyes so that they look half shut, and someone has pressed a copper coin into the mouth, now green with age.

8614.description: The shield bears a crown above a single open eye, the old sign of the king's foresters. Beneath it are cut the words THE ROAD IS THE KING'S PEACE, and travellers have rubbed the crown bright for luck.

8609.description: The little stag is carved from pale stone with great care, every tine of its antlers sharp, and the sun between them is inlaid with a disc of yellow glass. Foresters say the white stag of the Radiant Forest shows itself only to those who leave the woods as they found them.

8727.description: The lintel slab is carved with a row of spirals and a single line of runes too worn to read. Someone has wedged a twist of rowan into a crack above the door, and it has long since withered.

8679.description: The face is calm and heavy-lidded, its hair bound in a fillet of carved leaves. Someone has painted the eyes black, and not long ago, for the paint still shines.

8688.description: The temple's walls are of a black stone found nowhere else in the city, fitted without mortar. Above the grate a line of old script is cut into the lintel, and beneath it someone has scratched a plainer warning: WHAT IS GIVEN TO THE DARK IS NOT GIVEN BACK.

8654.description: The stone is clear yellow quartz, warm as a hand, and deep inside it hang specks of gold like motes in a sunbeam. Pilgrims have pressed their palms against it so often that one face is polished to a mirror.

creatures.long_desc: A white stag stands among the golden trees, watching you with calm dark eyes.
creatures.description: A tall stag with a coat as white as new snow and antlers that shine faintly gold where the light catches them. He holds his head high and still, and seems less afraid of you than curious. The foresters say it is ill luck to harm him.
rooms: The Edge of the Path of Light
A Trail Through A Light Forest
At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest
A Corner In The Radiant Forest

creatures.long_desc: A big brown bear shambles through the undergrowth, sniffing the air.
creatures.description: A heavy brown bear, its shaggy coat flecked with burrs and bracken, with a hump of muscle across its shoulders and claws as long as fingers. Its small eyes are short-sighted but its nose misses nothing, and it does not like to be disturbed at its foraging.

creatures.long_desc: A giant web spider hangs head-down among the branches, its many eyes glittering.
creatures.description: A spider the size of a small pony, with a bloated black body patterned in faint grey bands and legs furred with bristles. Its cluster of eyes gleams like wet beads, and its fangs drip a thin, clear venom. Strands of fresh silk trail behind it wherever it goes.
rooms: A Small Road In The Old Forest
On A Small Road In The Old Forest
On A Small Road In Old The Forest
The Edge Of The Old Forest

creatures.long_desc: A hulking bog troll squats in the mire, picking its teeth with a splinter of bone.
creatures.description: A stooped, long-armed brute twice the height of a man, its warty grey-green hide caked with peat and hung with strands of marsh weed. Its nose is long and drooping, its eyes small and red, and it smells powerfully of stagnant water. It carries a knotted club of black bog oak.

creatures.long_desc: A tomb robber crouches among the ruins, prying at a loose stone with a crowbar.
creatures.description: A lean, grimy man in a dark hooded coat with many pockets, a coil of rope over one shoulder and a shuttered lantern at his belt. His fingernails are black with grave dirt, and his eyes keep straying to the sealed temple at the heart of the ruins. He does not mean to share whatever he finds.
rooms: At The Centre Of The Ruins

creatures.long_desc: A shadow wraith drifts between the black trees, cold and silent.
creatures.description: A tall shape of darkness in the rough form of a cloaked man, its edges fraying into the gloom like smoke. Where its face should be there is only a deeper shadow and two pinpricks of pale light. The air around it is bitterly cold, and frost forms on the leaves where it passes.

creatures.long_desc: A village watchman walks his round, a lantern in one hand and a braid of garlic at his belt.
creatures.description: A sturdy, grey-whiskered villager in a padded jerkin, carrying a stout ash staff and an unlit lantern. A braid of garlic and a little tin sun hang from his belt, and he keeps glancing at the sky to judge how long is left until dusk. He nods to travellers, but he does not linger on the road.

items.room_desc: A pale antler, faintly gleaming gold at its tips, lies here.
items.description: A long, many-tined antler, smooth and creamy white, its tips touched with a faint golden sheen. Carvers in Garathorm prize such antlers for knife hilts, though the foresters of the Radiant Forest would ask hard questions about how you came by it.

items.short_desc: a skein of giant spider silk
items.room_desc: A skein of grey, gleaming spider silk lies here.
items.description: A tangled skein of silk from a giant spider, grey and gleaming and stronger than any rope of the same thickness. Weavers and bowyers will pay well for it, once the last of the sticky coating has been boiled away.

items.room_desc: A heavy club of black bog oak lies here, crusted with peat.
items.description: A great club cut from bog oak that lay for centuries in the marsh, its wood turned black and hard as iron. The head is a mass of knots, and the grip has been worn smooth by a hand much larger than yours.

items.room_desc: A small lantern with sliding iron shutters lies here.
items.description: A small brass lantern fitted with sliding iron shutters, so that its light can be narrowed to a thin beam or hidden altogether at the sound of footsteps. Its glass is smoked from long use in dark places.

items.short_desc: a cold band of black iron
items.room_desc: A plain ring of black iron lies here, rimed with frost.
items.description: A plain band of black iron, so cold that it mists the air around it, though it seems to drink in the warmth of the hand that wears it and give back a strange vigour. Tiny letters inside the band have been worn away to nothing.
